name: Brigadeiro
shortDescription: Chocolate Brazilian truffles made with condensed milk.
ingredients: 7 tablespoons chocolate drink mix or 4 tablespoons cocoa powder
instructions: Add the condensed milk, margarine, and chocolate powder to a deep pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until the mixture starts to pull away from the bottom of the pan.
Let it cool.
Roll the mixture into small balls and cover them with chocolate sprinkles.

name: Pão de Queijo
shortDescription: Cheesy Brazilian bread rolls.
ingredients: 350 g grated meia cura cheese or mozzarella
instructions: Heat the milk and oil in a pan and turn off the heat as soon as it starts to boil.
In a large bowl, mix the tapioca starch and salt.
Pour the hot milk and oil mixture into the bowl and mix first with a spoon, then with your hands.
Add the grated parmesan, some of the other cheese, and 1 egg, then keep mixing.
Add the rest of the cheese and check the texture of the dough.
If the dough is too dry, add another egg. If it is too oily, add a little more tapioca starch.
Shape the dough into small balls and place them on a baking sheet.
Bake at 230°C until lightly golden.

name: Pudim
shortDescription: Brazilian condensed milk flan.
ingredients: 1 can milk, using the condensed milk can as measurement
instructions: Blend the eggs well in a blender.
Add the condensed milk and milk, then blend again.
Melt the sugar in a pan until it turns golden brown.
Add the water and let the caramel thicken.
Pour the caramel into a round pan and add the pudding mixture on top.
Bake in a water bath for about 45 minutes.
Check with a fork to see if it is fully baked.
Let it cool and remove from the pan.

name: Cocada
shortDescription: A traditional coconut sweet with a chewy texture.
instructions: In a medium pan, mix the sugar and water carefully.
Cook over medium heat without stirring for about 20 minutes, until the syrup reaches a thin thread point.
Add the coconut and mix just enough to coat it with the syrup.
Cook for 5 more minutes over medium heat without stirring too much.
Transfer the cocada to a bowl and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Grease a baking sheet with butter.
Use two spoons to shape small portions and place them on the baking sheet.
Let them dry at room temperature for about 1 hour before serving.

name: Quindim
shortDescription: A glossy Brazilian dessert made with egg yolks and coconut.
instructions: In a bowl, add the sugar and coconut milk.
Mix with a spoon.
Add the coconut and mix again.
Add the egg yolks and mix everything by hand.
Pour the mixture into small molds greased with margarine and sugar.
Leave about 1 teaspoon of sugar at the bottom of each mold to create the shiny top.
Bake in a preheated oven in a water bath for about 1 hour.
Check with a toothpick. If it comes out dry, the quindim is ready.

name: Pamonha
shortDescription: A soft corn-based Brazilian dish often served sweet.
instructions: Grate the corn or cut the kernels from the cob and blend with water.
Add the coconut and sugar, then mix well.
Place the mixture inside the corn husks and tie them well.
In a large pot, bring water to a full boil.
Add the pamonhas one by one after the water is boiling.
Cook for about 40 minutes.
Remove them with a slotted spoon and let them cool in a fresh place.

name: Bolinha de Queijo
shortDescription: Small fried cheese balls that are popular as snacks.
instructions: Gather all the ingredients.
Place all ingredients in a bowl and mix well until a moldable dough forms.
Take small portions of the dough and shape them into balls.
Place the balls on a tray.
Freeze them for 30 minutes.
Fry the cheese balls in very hot oil.
Let them drain on paper towels before serving.

name: Empada
shortDescription: A small Brazilian savory pie with a soft crust.
ingredients: 500 g cooked and shredded chicken breast
1 dessert spoon chopped green bell pepper
instructions: Place the dough ingredients in a large bowl and mix well, adding the flour little by little until a smooth dough forms.
If the dough is too sticky, add more flour. If it is too dry, add more butter or margarine.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let it rest while preparing the filling.
Sauté the onion, garlic, tomato, and bell pepper in olive oil.
Add the shredded chicken and sauté a little more.
Add the flour and mix well.
Add the milk all at once and stir quickly.
Add the peas, salt, and parsley. When the filling thickens, turn off the heat and set aside.
Line small molds with the dough, pressing it against the bottom and sides.
Fill the molds with the cooled filling and add one olive to each empada.
Cover with dough circles and press the edges.
Brush with beaten egg yolk and bake for about 20 minutes, or until golden.
Let them cool before removing from the molds.

name: Farofa
shortDescription: Toasted cassava flour dish often served as a side.
instructions: Cut the bacon and calabresa sausage into cubes.
Add 1 tablespoon of oil to a pan and fry the bacon well.
Add the calabresa and fry until browned.
Add the chopped onion and garlic.
Let everything fry for a little longer.
Add the grated carrot.
Add the seasoning mix.
Add the cassava flour and mix well.

name: Strogonoff
shortDescription: Brazilian-style chicken strogonoff served with rice and potato sticks.
instructions: In a bowl, mix the chicken, garlic, mayonnaise, salt, and black pepper.
In a large skillet, melt the butter and brown the onion.
Add the seasoned chicken and cook until golden.
Add the mushrooms, ketchup, and mustard.
Mix in the heavy cream and remove from the heat before it starts boiling.
Serve with white rice and potato sticks.

name: Beijinho
shortDescription: A small Brazilian coconut sweet made with condensed milk.
instructions: Add the condensed milk, grated coconut, and margarine to a pan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until the mixture becomes thick and pulls away from the bottom of the pan.
Let it cool.
Roll the mixture into small balls.
Cover the balls with sugar or grated coconut.

name: Enroladinho de Salsicha
shortDescription: Small baked sausage rolls wrapped in soft dough.
instructions: In a bowl, mix the flour, butter, salt, milk, and baking powder.
Add more flour little by little if needed.
Open the dough and cut it into small rectangles.
Cut the sausages into 3 pieces and place them on the dough rectangles.
Roll the dough around the sausage pieces.
Place the rolls on a greased and floured baking sheet.
Brush each roll with egg yolk and oregano.
Bake at 180°C for about 30 minutes.

name: Bolinho de Espinafre
shortDescription: Small spinach fritters made with simple seasoning and flour.
ingredients: Parsley and green onions to taste
instructions: Boil the spinach briefly in a pot with water.
Chop the onion, garlic, and parsley, then season with salt.
Squeeze the spinach to remove extra water and chop it.
In a pan, sauté the spinach with the other seasonings.
Add the flour and cornstarch until the mixture becomes a firm dough.
Shape the mixture into small fritters.
Heat enough oil to cover the fritters.
Fry until golden.

name: Mousse de Limão
shortDescription: A creamy Brazilian lime mousse made with condensed milk.
instructions: Blend the condensed milk and heavy cream for about 3 minutes.
Slowly add the lime juice and keep blending.
Pour the mousse into a serving dish.
Refrigerate until firm.
Before serving, crush the Bis chocolate and sprinkle it on top.

name: Arroz Doce
shortDescription: A creamy Brazilian rice pudding with cinnamon and condensed milk.
instructions: Cook the rice with the milk and cinnamon in a large pot.
Use a large pot so the milk does not spill when it boils.
After 20 minutes, stir from time to time.
Add the sugar and cook for 20 more minutes.
Add the condensed milk and cook for another 20 minutes.
Transfer to a serving dish.

name: Pé de Moleque
shortDescription: A traditional Brazilian peanut sweet made with sugar and condensed milk.
instructions: Toast the peanuts and remove the skins.
Place the peanuts in a pan and add the sugar and condensed milk.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until the mixture starts to pull away from the bottom of the pan.
Pour the mixture into a pan greased with oil.
Let it cool a little.
Cut into small squares.

name: Palha Italiana
shortDescription: A Brazilian chocolate sweet made with brigadeiro and crushed cookies.
ingredients: 1 package Maria cookies or cornstarch cookies
instructions: Break the cookies into small pieces and set aside.
Make a brigadeiro using the condensed milk, margarine, and chocolate powder.
When the brigadeiro starts to pull away from the bottom of the pan, mix in the chopped cookies.
Remove from the heat.
Grease a smooth surface with margarine and spread the mixture over it.
Flatten the mixture with your hands.
Let it cool and cut into small squares.

name: Maçã do Amor
shortDescription: Brazilian candy apples covered with a red sugar glaze.
instructions: Wash and dry the apples.
Insert one or two sticks into each apple to make them firm enough for dipping.
Grease aluminum pans with a small amount of oil.
Place all the syrup ingredients in a pan.
Mix only by moving the pan, without using a spoon, so the syrup does not crystallize.
Cook over high heat until it boils, then lower to medium heat for about 25 minutes.
Test the syrup by dropping a little onto the pan. If it hardens and makes a solid sound, turn off the heat.
Quickly dip the apples into the syrup.
Place the apples on the greased pan before the syrup hardens.

name: Creme de Milho
shortDescription: A creamy Brazilian corn side dish made with milk and cream.
instructions: Blend the corn with the milk until smooth.
In a pan, heat the butter and sauté the onion until lightly golden.
Add the flour and stir quickly to create a creamy base.
Add the blended corn and the vegetable bouillon cube.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until it thickens.
Add the heavy cream, mix well, and turn off the heat.

name: Coxinha de Frango
shortDescription: A popular Brazilian fried snack filled with seasoned shredded chicken.
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the onion and garlic until golden.
Add the chicken, tomato, and olives, and cook for a few minutes.
Mix in the requeijao and parsley, season with salt and black pepper, and set aside.
For the dough, bring the water, margarine, salt, and black pepper to a boil in a pan.
Add the corn flour and cornstarch all at once, stirring well until the dough pulls away from the bottom.
Transfer the dough to a smooth surface and let it cool slightly before kneading.
Open small portions of dough in your hand and place some filling inside.
Close and shape the coxinhas.
Dip them in beaten eggs and then coat them with flaked corn flour.
Fry in hot oil until golden and drain on paper towels.

name: Risoles de Carne Moída
shortDescription: Brazilian fried turnovers filled with seasoned ground beef.
instructions: Peel and dice the onion, crush the garlic, and separate all the ingredients.
For the filling, heat the oil in a pan and add the ground beef, letting it brown before stirring.
When the beef changes color, add the onion, garlic, salt, paprika, black pepper, and tomato paste.
Cook until the filling is fully cooked and set aside.
For the dough, place the milk, water, chicken bouillon, margarine, and salt in a pan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and gradually add the flour, stirring until a dough forms.
Cook the dough for about 5 to 10 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a counter and knead with the help of a rolling pin until it cools.
Open small discs of dough, fill them with the ground beef, and close the risoles tightly.
To coat them, mix the eggs, water, and salt in one bowl and place the breadcrumbs in another.
Dip the risoles in the egg mixture and then in the breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil until golden and drain on paper towels.

name: Pão de Alho
shortDescription: Brazilian garlic bread made with cheese, garlic, and mayonnaise.
instructions: Gather all the ingredients.
In a bowl, mix the mayonnaise, garlic, butter or margarine, parmesan, mozzarella, and herbs.
Make cuts in the bread, being careful not to cut all the way through.
Spread the garlic mixture inside each cut and over the top.
Bake in the air fryer for 10 minutes at 200°C, or in the oven for about 20 to 25 minutes at the same temperature.
Serve warm.

name: Biscoito de Polvilho
shortDescription: A light and crispy Brazilian baked cassava starch biscuit.
instructions: In a bowl, combine the cassava starch, boiling water, and oil.
Mix well and add salt to taste.
Add the eggs one at a time until the dough becomes consistent.
Place the dough in a piping bag and shape the biscuits on a baking tray.
There is no need to grease the tray.
Bake in a preheated medium oven at 180°C for about 25 minutes.
